reason: No prior evidence is cited for any of the key premises. The hypothesis relies entirely on textbook knowledge of HfO2 properties and unsupported assumptions about coating behavior on this specific substrate in molten aluminum.
premises: Hf coating oxidizes to form a dense, adherent HfO2 scale in molten Al at ~700°C
HfO2 scale is chemically inert and impervious to molten Al
HfO2 scale prevents Al penetration and reaction with the underlying boride
A ~100 μm PVD Hf coating can form such a protective scale on a high-entropy boride substrate
